legend: At first, there was a legend related to the name of the problem, but now it's just a formal statement.
You are given n%%ZSMJ0%% points a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ1%% on the OX%%ZSMJ2%% axis. Now you are asked to find such an integer point x%%ZSMJ3%% on OX%%ZSMJ4%% axis that fk(x)%%ZSMJ5%% is minimal possible.
The function fk(x)%%ZSMJ6%% can be described in the following way:
form a list of distances d1,d2,…,dn%%ZSMJ7%% where di=|ai−x|%%ZSMJ8%% (distance between ai%%ZSMJ9%% and x%%ZSMJ10%%);
sort list d%%ZSMJ11%% in non-descending order;
If there are multiple optimal answers you can print any of them.
input: The first line contains single integer T%%ZSMJ13%% (1≤T≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ14%%) — number of queries. Next 2⋅T%%ZSMJ15%% lines contain descriptions of queries. All queries are independent.
The first line of each query contains two integers n%%ZSMJ16%%, k%%ZSMJ17%% (1≤n≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ18%%, 0≤k<n%%ZSMJ19%%) — the number of points and constant k%%ZSMJ20%%.
The second line contains n%%ZSMJ21%% integers a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ22%% (1≤a1<a2<⋯<an≤109%%ZSMJ23%%) — points in ascending order.
output: Print T%%ZSMJ26%% integers — corresponding points x%%ZSMJ27%% which have minimal possible value of fk(x)%%ZSMJ28%%. If there are multiple answers you can print any of them.
